title: Fleetly Fleet Management Dashboard
one_liner: A dense, glanceable dashboard that gives operations managers real-time insight into fleet performance and alerts.
audience: Operations managers overseeing commercial fleets who need to monitor vehicle status, deliveries, and issues at a glance.
concept: The design centers on a high‑density command‑center layout where the most critical metrics occupy the top row, a live map visualizes vehicle distribution, and a sortable table surfaces actionable details. The sky‑blue accent highlights interactive elements and active states, while a clean Inter typeface and ample whitespace ensure readability despite the information density. Dark and light modes share the same spatial hierarchy, letting users switch contexts without relearning the layout.

palette.notes: Light mode values shown; dark mode inverts bg/#0F172A, surface/#1E293B, text/#F8FAFC, muted/#94A3B8 while keeping primary accent #0EA5E9 for contrast.

typography.notes: Inter used for both headings and body; weights: semibold for headings, regular for body; tabular-nums applied to numbers.

layout: Uses an 8px grid; fixed sidebar 260px wide (collapsible to 80px on <640px); top bar 64px; sections spaced with py-6 md:py-8; cards employ radius-md (12px) and shadow-sm with hover lift -translate-y-1; motion includes 150ms hover/focus transitions and fade‑in reveal on load, respecting prefers-reduced-motion.

sections.goal: Show key fleet metrics at a glance
sections.content: Four statistic cards: Active Vehicles (number), Deliveries Today (number), Avg Delivery Time (minutes), Alerts (count with badge). Each card displays a large numeric value, label, and an inline SVG icon.
A map placeholder (800px width, 400px height) rendered with SVG grid lines and animated dots representing vehicles; includes a status-color legend and a refresh button.

Table with columns Plate Number, Driver, Status, Last Location, Fuel Level; status shown as colored pill; includes a global search input above the table and sortable column headers with SVG sort arrows.

copy_voice: Clear, concise, professional; uses imperative labels and units; avoids jargon; focuses on actionable data.
imagery: No stock photos; all visuals are CSS/SVG: map uses an SVG grid with animated dots; stat cards and table use inline Lucide‑style icons (stroke 1.75); status pills are colored divs; hover states use subtle transforms.
must_avoid: Hardcoded pixel values that break the 8px grid
Overly bold colors that reduce readability
Complex charts that distract from core data
